result.rule: When the description makes a later step conditional on another party's approval or acceptance of an earlier deliverable, and it does not spell out a separate negative outcome: Model an exclusive gateway at the approval point. Give the approved flow a condition and route it to the next activity. Give a second outgoing flow with a condition for the not-approved case, leading to an end event or back to the deliverable, depending on what the description supports. Do not leave the approval as a plain sequence without a gateway.

When the description states that a review or assessment by one party leads to an approval, that the approval itself is performed work by that party, and that the approved outcome is then carried out through several separately described actions (for example, one that changes duties and another that changes pay), each given its own sentence: Model the approval as its own task performed by the stated party, placed after the review and before the approved branch. Then model each separately described follow-up action as its own task, in the order or concurrency the description gives, after the approval. Do not leave the approval implicit in the gateway label, and do not merge the follow-up actions into one combined task.

When the description states that an activity is performed on selected items, and only afterwards does the process branch according to a choice that each item states about how the next step is carried out: Model the stated activity as its own task, placed after the preceding step and connected to it by a sequence flow. Place the decision gateway after that task, not directly after the preceding step, so that the stated activity appears in the model and the branches are driven by the condition each item states.

When the description states that a set of selected items each receive a follow-up activity, and a later choice then branches according to an attribute of each item: Model the follow-up activity as its own task on the sequence path that leads to the decision, placed after the step that selects the items and before the decision gateway. Place the exclusive gateway after that task, with one conditioned outgoing flow per alternative, and do not skip the follow-up task or attach the decision directly to the selection step.
